`.mcp.json` at the project root (project-scoped) or in `~/.claude.json` (user-scoped).\r\n\r\n### Server Types\r\n\r\n| Type | Transport | Example |\r\n|------|-----------|---------|\r\n| **stdio** | Spawns a local process | `npx`, `python`, binary |\r\n| **http** | Connects to a remote URL | HTTP/SSE endpoint |\r\n\r\n### Example `.mcp.json`\r\n\r\n```json\r\n{\r\n  \"mcpServers\": {\r\n    \"context7\": {\r\n      \"command\": \"npx\",\r\n      \"args\": [\"-y\", \"@upstash/context7-mcp\"]\r\n    },\r\n    \"playwright\": {\r\n      \"command\": \"npx\",\r\n      \"args\": [\"-y\", \"@playwright/mcp\"]\r\n    },\r\n    \"deepwiki\": {\r\n      \"command\": \"npx\",\r\n      \"args\": [\"-y\", \"deepwiki-mcp\"]\r\n    },\r\n    \"remote-api\": {\r\n      \"type\": \"http\",\r\n      \"url\": \"https://mcp.example.com/mcp\"\r\n    }\r\n  }\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\nUse environment variable expansion for secrets instead of committing API keys in `.mcp.json`:\r\n\r\n```json\r\n{\r\n  \"mcpServers\": {\r\n    \"remote-api\": {\r\n      \"type\": \"http\",\r\n      \"url\": \"https://mcp.example.com/mcp?token=${MCP_API_TOKEN}\"\r\n    }\r\n  }\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\n### Settings for MCP Servers\r\n\r\nThese settings in `.claude/settings.json` control MCP server approval:\r\n\r\n| Key | Type | Description |\r\n|-----|------|-------------|\r\n| `enableAllProjectMcpServers` | boolean | Auto-approve all `.mcp.json` servers without prompting |\r\n| `enabledMcpjsonServers` | array | Allowlist of specific server names to auto-approve |\r\n| `disabledMcpjsonServers` | array | Blocklist of specific server names to reject |\r\n\r\n### Permission Rules for MCP Tools\r\n\r\nMCP tools follow the `mcp__<server>__<tool>` naming convention in permission rules:\r\n\r\n```json\r\n{\r\n  \"permissions\": {\r\n    \"allow\": [\r\n      \"mcp__*\",\r\n      \"mcp__context7__*\",\r\n      \"mcp__playwright__browser_snapshot\"\r\n    ],\r\n    \"deny\": [\r\n      \"mcp__dangerous-server__*\"\r\n    ]\r\n  }\r\n}\r\n```\n\n### eee-mcp-json (2)\n{\n  \"_comment\": \"Wave 75 2026-05-08 — Tier-2A HTTP MCPs (github + context7 + deepwiki) + kits-convergence stdio Accepts aliases (`sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`) or full model IDs |\r\n| `agent` | string | - | Set the default agent for the main conversation. Value is the agent name from `.claude/agents/`. Inactive session transcripts and orphaned subagent worktrees are deleted; as of v2.1.117 the sweep also covers `~/.claude/tasks/`, `~/.claude/shell-snapshots/`, and `~/.claude/backups/`. Setting to `0` is rejected with a validation error. To disable transcript writes in non-interactive mode (`-p`), use `--no-session-persistence` or `persistSession: false` SDK option |\r\n| `autoUpdatesChannel` | string | `\"latest\"` | Release channel: `\"stable\"` or `\"latest\"` |\r\n| `minimumVersion` | string | - | Prevent the auto-updater from downgrading below a specific version. Automatically set when switching to the stable channel and choosing to stay on the current version until stable catches up. Used with `autoUpdatesChannel` |\r\n| `alwaysThinkingEnabled` | boolean | `false` | Enable extended thinking by default for all sessions |\r\n| `skipWebFetchPreflight` | boolean | `false` | Skip WebFetch blocklist check before fetching URLs *(in JSON schema, not on official settings page)* |\r\n| `availableModels` | array | - | Restrict which models users can select via `/model`, `--model`, Config tool, or `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`. Does not affect the Default option. Example: `[\"sonnet\", \"haiku\"]` |\r\n| `fastModePerSessionOptIn` | boolean | `false` | Require users to opt in to fast mode each session |\r\n| `defaultShell` | string | `\"bash\"` | Default shell for input-box `!` commands. Accepts `\"bash\"` (default) or `\"powershell\"`. Setting `\"powershell\"` routes interactive `!` commands through PowerShell on Windows. Also configurable via `env` key — see [Settings Reference](./claude-settings.md#environment-variables-via-env) |\r\n| `CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD=1` | Enable additional directory CLAUDE.md loading |\r\n| `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1` | Disable auto-updates. Also configurable via `env` key — see [Settings Reference](./claude-settings.md#environment-variables-via-env) |\r\n| `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL` | Control thinking depth — see [Settings Reference](./claude-settings.md#environment-variables-via-env) |\r\n| `USE_BUILTIN_RIPGREP=0` | Use system ripgrep instead of built-in (Alpine Linux) |\r\n| `CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE` | Enable simple mode (Bash + Edit tools only). Also configurable via `env` key — see [Settings Reference](./claude-settings.md#environment-variables-via-env) |\r\n| `CLAUDE_BASH_NO_LOGIN=1` | Skip login shell for BashTool |\r\n| `CCR_FORCE_BUNDLE=1` | Force bundling/uploading local repository when using `claude --remote`. Also configurable via `env` key — see [Settings Reference](./claude-settings.md#environment-variables-via-env) |\r\n\r\nFor environment variables configurable via the `\"env\"` key in `settings.json` (including `MAX_THINKING_TOKENS`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL`, `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TASKS`, `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS`, `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS`, and more), see the [Claude Settings Reference](./claude-settings.md#environment-variables-via-env).\n\n### ccbp-claude-commands-full\n## Frontmatter Fields (15)\r\n\r\n| Field | Type | Required | Description |\r\n|-------|------|----------|-------------|\r\n| `name` | string | No | Display name and `/slash-command` identifier. Defaults to the directory name if omitted |\r\n| `description` | string | Recommended | What the command does. Shown in autocomplete and used by Claude for auto-discovery |\r\n| `when_to_use` | string | No | Additional context for when Claude should invoke the skill — trigger phrases or example requests. Appended to `description` in the listing and counts toward the 1,536-character cap |\r\n| `argument-hint` | string | No | Hint shown during autocomplete (e.g., `[issue-number]`, `[filename]`) |\r\n| `arguments` | string/list | No | Named positional arguments for `$name` substitution in command content. Accepts a space-separated string or YAML list — names map to argument positions in order |\r\n| `disable-model-invocation` | boolean | No | Set `true` to prevent Claude from automatically invoking this command |\r\n| `user-invocable` | boolean | No | Set `false` to hide from the `/` menu — command becomes background knowledge only |\r\n| `paths` | string/list | No | Glob patterns that limit when this skill is activated. Accepts a comma-separated string or a YAML list. When set, Claude loads the skill automatically only when working with files matching the patterns |\r\n| `allowed-tools` | string | No | Tools allowed without permission prompts when this command is active |\r\n| `model` | string | No | Model to use when this command runs (e.g., `haiku`, `sonnet`, `opus`) |\r\n| `effort` | string | No | Override the model effort level when invoked (`low`, `medium`, `high`, `max`) |\r\n| `context` | string | No | Set to `fork` to run the command in an isolated subagent context |\r\n| `agent` | string | No | Subagent type when `context: fork` is set (default: `general-purpose`) |\r\n| `shell` | string | No | Shell for `` !`command` `` blocks — accepts `bash` (default) or `powershell`. ccbp-claude-memory-full\n….com/bcherny/status/2016339448863355206\"><img src=\"assets/claude-memory/claude-memory-monorepo.jpg\" alt=\"CLAUDE.md loading in monorepos\" width=\"600\"></a>\r\n</p>\r\n\r\n### The Two Loading Mechanisms\r\n\r\nClaude Code uses two distinct mechanisms for loading CLAUDE.md files:\r\n\r\n#### Ancestor Loading (UP the directory tree)\r\n\r\nWhen you start Claude Code, it walks **upward** from your current working directory toward the filesystem root and loads every CLAUDE.md it finds along the way. These files are loaded **immediately at startup**.\r\n\r\n#### Descendant Loading (DOWN the directory tree)\r\n\r\nCLAUDE.md files in subdirectories below your current working directory are **NOT loaded at launch**. They are only included when Claude reads files in those subdirectories during your session. This is known as **lazy loading**.\r\n\r\n### Example Monorepo Structure\r\n\r\nConsider a typical monorepo with separate directories for different components:\r\n\r\n```\r\n/mymonorepo/\r\n├── CLAUDE.md          # Root-level instructions (shared across all components)\r\n├── frontend/\r\n│   └── CLAUDE.md      # Frontend-specific instructions\r\n├── backend/\r\n│   └── CLAUDE.md      # Backend-specific instructions\r\n└── api/\r\n    └── CLAUDE.md      # API-specific instructions\r\n```\r\n\r\n### Scenario 1: Running Claude Code from the Root Directory\r\n\r\nWhen you run Claude Code from `/mymonorepo/`:\r\n\r\n```bash\r\ncd /mymonorepo\r\nclaude\r\n```\r\n\r\n| File | Loaded at Launch? | Reason |\r\n|------|-------------------|--------|\r\n| `/mymonorepo/CLAUDE.md` | Yes | It's your current working directory |\r\n| `/mymonorepo/frontend/CLAUDE.md` | No | Loaded only when you read/edit files in `frontend/` |\r\n| `/mymonorepo/backend/CLAUDE.md` | No | Loaded only when you read/edit files in `backend/` |\r\n| `/mymonorepo/api/CLAUDE.md` | No | Loaded only when you read/edit files in `api/` |\r\n\r\n### Scenario 2: Running Claude Code from a Component Directory\r\n\r\nWhen you run Claude Code from `/mymonorepo/frontend/`:\r\n\r\n```bash\r\ncd /mymonorepo/frontend\r\nclaude\r\n```\r\n\r\n| File | Loaded at Launch? | Reason |\r\n|------|-------------------|--------|\r\n| `/mymonorepo/CLAUDE.md` | Yes | It's an ancestor directory |\r\n| `/mymonorepo/frontend/CLAUDE.md` | Yes | It's your current working directory |\r\n| `/mymonorepo/backend/CLAUDE.md` | No | Different branch of the directory tree |\r\n| `/mymonorepo/api/CLAUDE.md` | No | Different branch of the directory tree |\r\n\r\n### Key Takeaways\r\n\r\n1. **Ancestors always load at startup** — Claude walks UP the directory tree and loads all CLAUDE.md files it finds. This ensures you always have access to root-level, repository-wide instructions.\r\n\r\n2. **Descendants load lazily** — Subdirectory CLAUDE.md files only load when you interact with files in those subdirectories. This prevents irrelevant context fr…\n\n…s regardless of project.\r\n\r\n### Why This Design Works for Monorepos\r\n\r\n- **Shared instructions propagate down** — Root-level CLAUDE.md contains repository-wide conventions, coding standards, and common patterns that apply ever…\n\n### ccbp-claude-startup-flags-full\n## Directory & Workspace\r\n\r\n| Flag | Short | Description ccbp-claude-mcp-full\\n## Configuration\\r\\n\\r\\nMCP servers are configured in `.mcp.json` at the project root (project-scoped) or in `~/.claude.json` (user-scoped).\\r\\n\\r\\n### Server Types\\r\\n\\r\\n| Type | Transport | Example |\\r\\n|------|-----------|---------|\\r\\n| **stdio** | Spawns a local process | `npx`, `python`, binary |\\r\\n| **http** | Connects to a remote URL | \\\"remote-api\\\": {\\r\\n      \\\"type\\\": \\\"http\\\",\\r\\n      \\\"url\\\": \\\"https://mcp.example.com/mcp\\\"\\r\\n    }\\r\\n  }\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nUse environment variable `.claude/settings.json` control MCP server approval:\\r\\n\\r\\n| Key | Type | Description |\\r\\n|-----|------|-------------|\\r\\n| `enableAllProjectMcpServers` | boolean | Auto-approve all `.mcp.json` servers without prompting |\\r\\n| `enabledMcpjsonServers` | array | Allowlist of specific server names to auto-approve |\\r\\n| `disabledMcpjsonServers` | array | Blocklist of specific server names to reject |\\r\\n\\r\\n### Permission Rules for MCP Tools\\r\\n\\r\\nMCP tools follow the `mcp__<server>__<tool>` naming convention in permission rules:\\r\\n\\r\\n```json\\r\\n{\\r\\n ccbp-claude-mcp-full\\n## Configuration\\r\\n\\r\\nMCP servers are configured in `.mcp.json` at the project root (project-scoped) or in `~/.claude.json` (user-scoped).\\r\\n\\r\\n### Server Types\\r\\n\\r\\n| Type | Transport | Example |\\r\\n|------|-----------|---------|\\r\\n| **stdio** | Spawns a local process | `npx`, `python`, binary |\\r\\n| **http** | Connects to a remote URL | HTTP/SSE endpoint |\\r\\n\\r\\n### Example `.mcp.json`\\r\\n\\r\\n```json\\r\\n{\\r\\n  \\\"mcpServers\\\": {\\r\\n    \\\"context7\\\": {\\r\\n      \\\"command\\\": \\\"npx\\\",\\r\\n      \\\"args\\\": [\\\"-y\\\", \\\"@upstash/context7-mcp\\\"]\\r\\n    },\\r\\n    \\\"playwright\\\": {\\r\\n      \\\"command\\\": \\\"npx\\\",\\r\\n      \\\"args\\\": [\\\"-y\\\", \\\"@playwright/mcp\\\"]\\r\\n    },\\r\\n    \\\"deepwiki\\\": {\\r\\n      \\\"command\\\": \\\"npx\\\",\\r\\n      \\\"args\\\": [\\\"-y\\\", \\\"deepwiki-mcp\\\"]\\r\\n    },\\r\\n    \\\"remote-api\\\": {\\r\\n      \\\"type\\\": \\\"http\\\",\\r\\n      \\\"url\\\": \\\"https://mcp.example.com/mcp\\\"\\r\\n    }\\r\\n  }\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nUse environment variable expansion for secrets instead of committing API keys in `.mcp.json`:\\r\\n\\r\\n```json\\r\\n{\\r\\n  \\\"mcpServers\\\": {\\r\\n    \\\"remote-api\\\": {\\r\\n      \\\"type\\\": \\\"http\\\",\\r\\n      \\\"url\\\": \\\"https://mcp.example.com/mcp?token=${MCP_API_TOKEN}\\\"\\r\\n    }\\r\\n  }\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n### Settings for MCP Servers\\r\\n\\r\\nThese settings in `.claude/settings.json` control MCP server approval:\\r\\n\\r\\n| Key | Type | Description |\\r\\n|-----|------|-------------|\\r\\n| `enableAllProjectMcpServers` | boolean | Auto-approve all `.mcp.json` servers without prompting |\\r\\n| `enabledMcpjsonServers` | array | Allowlist of specific server names to auto-approve |\\r\\n| `disabledMcpjsonServers` | array | Blocklist of specific server names to reject |\\r\\n\\r\\n### Permission Rules for MCP Tools\\r\\n\\r\\nMCP tools follow the `mcp__<server>__<tool>` naming convention in permission rules:\\r\\n\\r\\n```json\\r\\n{\\r\\n  \\\"permissions\\\": {\\r\\n    \\\"allow\\\": [\\r\\n      \\\"mcp__*\\\",\\r\\n      \\\"mcp__context7__*\\\",\\r\\n      \\\"mcp__playwright__browser_snapshot\\\"\\r\\n    ],\\r\\n    \\\"deny\\\": [\\r\\n      \\\"mcp__dangerous-server__*\\\"\\r\\n    ]\\r\\n  }\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\n\\n### eee-mcp-json (2)\\n{\\n  \\\"_comment\\\": \\\"Wave 75 2026-05-08 — Tier-2A HTTP MCPs (github + context7 + 2:name: deprecation-discipline
3:description: Code-as-liability sunset discipline. Sister to kiss-dry-yagni.md (prevents speculative ADD); this rule covers cleanup-phase REMOVAL + migration. Use when sunsetting features, replacing legacy systems, removing dead code that nobody owns but everybody depends on, OR planning lifecycle of new system at design time (deprecation planning starts at design time per Hyrum's Law).
9:# Reference: constituents=[TIER-1-DIRECT @ Z:/claude-sota-installed/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/addy-agent-skills/skills/deprecation-and-migration/SKILL.md:10-12 @742dca5, TIER-3-LOCAL-COMPOSITION @ claude-sota-installed adaptation]; effective_tier=TIER-3-LOCAL-COMPOSITION per citation-discipline.md rule #8 [VERIFIED 2026-05-08 via Wave 82m-B sota-researcher Top-3 CITE-IMPORT #2 + Wave 82x codex T1 NEEDS-REVISION fix-forward F-001 cite-class reframe] — addyosmani/agent-skills (33,500 stars MIT, named-author Addy Osmani / Google Chrome team). Upstream verbatim at SKILL.md:10-12: "Code is a liability, not an asset. Every line of code has ongoing maintenance cost — bugs to fix, dependencies to update, security patches to apply, and new engineers to onboard. Deprecation is the discipline of removing code that no longer earns its keep, and migration is the process of moving users safely from the old to the new."
11:# Reference: TIER-2 sister rule `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/karpathy-adapted.md §3 Surgical Changes` (cite-import-AMBER per Section 14.5) — "Don't refactor things that aren't broken" interacts with deprecation: leave non-broken UNLESS deprecation-decision triggers (see §The deprecation decision below).
25:5. Planning lifecycle of NEW system at design time ("how would we remove this in 3 years?")
32:This is why deprecation requires **active migration**, not just announcement. Users can't "just switch" when they depend on behaviors the replacement doesn't replicate.
34:## The deprecation decision (5-question gate)
36:Before deprecating ANY surface — code, API, plugin, MCP, hook, rule, agent, skill — answer these in order:
40:3. **Does a replacement exist?** → If no, build the replacement FIRST. Never deprecate without an alternative. **Replacement readiness gate** (per Wave 82x codex T1 fix-forward F-003 / upstream SKILL.md:71-75): replacement must (a) cover critical use cases of the old system, (b) have documentation + migration guides, AND (c) be proven in production (not just "theoretically better") before deprecation starts.
42:5. **What's the ongoing cost of NOT deprecating?** → Security risk + engineer time + opportunity cost of complexity.
44:## Compulsory vs advisory deprecation
48:| **Advisory** | Replacement exists, soft-migrate path acceptable | Documentation deprecation note + warning at use site + parallel-deploy + telemetry |
49:| **Compulsory** | Breaking change required (security, broken contract, blocking next-gen feature) AND maintenance cost or risk justifies forcing migration | Hard removal at version cut OR `@deprecated` + compile error path + migration grace window |
51:**Default to advisory.** Use compulsory only when maintenance cost or risk justifies forcing migration. Compulsory deprecation requires migration tooling, documentation, and support; a deadline alone is not sufficient. Per Wave 82x codex T1 fix-forward F-002: upstream Osmani SKILL.md:62-65 mandates default-to-advisory + compulsory-with-tooling guardrail.
58:4. **Removal**: delete old code, dependencies, docs, references — verify ZERO active usage via metrics/logs/dependency analysis (NOT just `rg "<old-symbol>"` text search; per Wave 82x codex T1 fix-forward F-005 / upstream SKILL.md:112-118,201-206); then remove tests + docs + config + deprecation notices
62:**If you own the surface being deprecated, you own user migration or backward-compatible updates; do not leave consumers to discover the path themselves.** Per Wave 82x codex T1 fix-forward F-004 / upstream SKILL.md:106. This makes the owner responsibility EXPLICIT — distinct from the "Announce-and-leave" anti-pattern below (which describes the failure mode this rule prevents).
66:- **Announce-and-leave**: emitting `@deprecated` without migration support — Hyrum's Law guarantees nobody migrates. Refuted by §Migration patterns 4-stage active discipline.
67:- **Hard-remove-without-replacement**: deprecating before a viable migration path exists. Refuted by §The deprecation decision question 3.
68:- **Maintain-forever**: keeping a legacy system because "users depend on it" without measuring the maintenance cost. Refuted by §The deprecation decision question 5.
69:- **Speculative-deprecation**: marking code `@deprecated` because "we might replace it someday". This violates kiss-dry-yagni — only deprecate when a real replacement exists. Sister to "speculative ADD" anti-pattern.
75:- `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/karpathy-adapted.md §3 Surgical Changes` (cite-import-AMBER) — "Don't refactor things that aren't broken" interacts with deprecation: leave non-broken UNLESS deprecation-decision triggers (Hyrum's Law catches false-non-broken cases)
76:- `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/research-protocol.md` 3 gates — RECALL → INVESTIGATE → VERIFY before deprecating any surface (verify replacement exists + dependents migrated)
77:- `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/codification-threshold.md` cycle-322 — symmetric: codification gate prevents premature ADD; deprecation gate prevents premature KEEP
89:- Osmani updates `deprecation-and-migration/SKILL.md` upstream — re-pin SHA + re-extract any new mechanics
90:- A 4th deprecation-class surface emerges in claude-sota-installed (currently 3 trigger conditions per §When this discipline applies — extend to 4+ if observed)
91:- Hyrum's Law violation costs >2h re-derive in any single fire — promote to mechanical-enforcement (e.g., consumer-graph audit hook before deprecation Edit)
93:- claude-sota-installed deprecates ANY existing primitive (plugin / MCP / rule / agent / hook) — apply this rule to that deprecation as its first dogfood
